# 1 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_007_page_001.jpg

---

1. In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius son of Seleucus came out from Rome and went up with a few men to a city by the sea, and he reigned there.
2. And it came to pass, as he was entering the royal house of his fathers, the army seized Antiochus and Lysias to bring them to him.
3. And when the matter was made known to him, he said, "Do not show me their face."
4. And the army slew them; and Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
5. And there came to him all the lawless men and ungodly men of Israel; and Alcimus, who wanted to be high priest, led them.
6. And they accused the people before the king, saying, "Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your friends and scattered us from our land.
7. Now therefore send a man whom you trust, and let him go and see all the destruction which he has wrought upon us and upon the land of the king, and let him punish them and all their helpers."
8. And the king chose Bacchides, one of the Friends of the king, who was ruling over the Great Plain, great and faithful to the king, and sent him.
9. And he sent with him the ungodly Alcimus, and confirmed to him the high priesthood, and commanded him to take vengeance on the sons of Israel.
10. And they set out and came with a great force to the land of Judah; and he sent messengers to Judas and his brothers with words of peace, deceitfully.
11. But they paid no attention to their words, for they saw that they came with a great force.
12. Then a company of scribes came together to Alcimus and Bacchides to ask for just dealings.
13. And the Hasideans were the first among the sons of Israel to seek peace with them; for they said, "A priest of the seed of Aaron has come with the armies, and he will not do us wrong."
14. And he spoke to them words of peace and swore to them, saying, "We will not seek evil against you or your friends."
15. And they trusted him; and he seized sixty of them and killed them in one day, according to the word which was written:
16. "The flesh of your holy ones and their blood they poured out around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
17. And fear and trembling fell upon all the people; for they said, "There is no truth and no judgment in them, for they broke their agreement and the oath which they swore."
18. And Bacchides departed from Jerusalem and encamped in Beth-zaith; and he sent and took many of those who had deserted him, and also some of the people, and killed them and threw them into the great cistern.
19. And he committed the land to Alcimus and left with him a force to help him; and Bacchides went to the king.
20. And Alcimus was struggling for his high priesthood.
21. And all who were troubling their people gathered to him, and they got the land of Judah into their power and did much hurt in Israel.
22. And Judas saw all the evil that Alcimus and those with him had done among the sons of Israel, evil worse than the nations.
23. And he went out into all the territory of Judea all around, and took vengeance on the men who had deserted, and they were restrained from going into the land.
24. But when Alcimus saw that Judas and those with him grew strong, and knew that he was not able to resist him, he returned to the king and accused them of many wrongs.
25. And the king sent Nicanor, one of his honored princes, who was an enemy and hated Israel, and commanded him to destroy the people.
26. And Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great force; and he sent to Judas and his brothers with words of peace deceitfully, saying,
27. "Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men so that we may see each other's faces in peace."
28. And he came to Judas, and they greeted each other peaceably; but the enemies were prepared to seize Judas.
29. And the matter became known to Judas that he had come to him with deceit; and he was afraid of him and would not see his face any more.
30. And Nicanor knew that his plan had been discovered; and he went out to meet Judas in battle near Capharsalama.
31. And about five hundred men of Nicanor's side fell; and they fled to the city of David.
32. And after these things Nicanor went up to Mount Zion; and certain of the priests out of the sanctuary and certain of the elders of the people came out to greet him in peace,
33. and to show him the burnt offering that was being offered on behalf of the king,
34. and he laughed at them and mocked them, and defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
35. And he swore with wrath, saying, "Unless Judas and his army are delivered into my hands, it shall come to pass, if ever I return in safety, that I will burn this house"; and he went out in great wrath.
36. And the priests entered and stood before the altar and the temple, and they wept and said:
37. "You chose this house to call your name upon it, to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people.
38. Take vengeance upon this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword; remember their blasphemies and do not let them endure."
39. And Nicanor departed from Jerusalem and encamped in Beth-horon; and the force of Syria met him.
40. And Judas encamped in Adasa with three thousand men; and Judas prayed and said:
41. "When the messengers of the king blasphemed, your angel went out and struck of them a hundred and eighty-five thousand.
42. In the same way, crush this army before us today, and let the rest know that he spoke evilly against your sanctuary; and judge him according to his wickedness."
43. And on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar the armies met in battle; and Nicanor's army was struck, and he himself was the first to fall in the battle.
44. And when his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
45. And the men of Judea pursued them a day's journey from Adasa, even to Gazara; and they sounded the signal trumpets after them.
46. And men came out of all the surrounding villages of Judea, and they flanked them around and turned them back on themselves, and they all fell by the sword; and there was not one of them left.
47. And they took the spoils and the plunder; and they cut off Nicanor's head and his right arm which he had stretched out with great pride, and they brought it and hung it up near Jerusalem.
48. And the people rejoiced greatly and kept that day as a day of great gladness.
49. And they ordained that this day should be observed every year on the thirteenth of Adar.
50. And the land of Judah was at rest for a little while.
